title: Forbidden Actions Registry
description: Canonical list of actions an automated agent MUST NOT perform without explicit per-action human authorisation. The default registry ships at .devai/config/forbidden-actions.json; adopters may extend but never relax it.

waivers.description: Explicit, reasoned exceptions for canonical protections this repository intentionally does not carry. A canonical id absent from both `actions` and `waivers` is an unwaived gap; extend the registry rather than silently dropping shipped protections.

id.description: The canonical FORBID-* id being waived.

reason.description: Why this repo does not carry this canonical protection. Forensic trail, not a rubber stamp.

action.description: Short imperative description, e.g. 'force-push to any branch'.

detect_patterns.description: Regex patterns (as strings) the scanner uses to detect violations in commit messages, recent commands, or reflog entries.

allowed_change_line_patterns.description: Optional exact development-context regexes. A detected commit-change occurrence is ignored only when its own changed line matches one of these patterns. Commit messages and other occurrences remain findings.

maintenance_exemptions.description: Optional registry-maintenance exemptions for this action (ADR-GOV-0022). Each item names one governed file whose validated, append-only change is maintenance rather than a mutation. A commit changes that path as maintenance only when the resulting file validates against the named schema and the change is append-only: every member of the parent version of the collection is present in the child version with identical bytes and in the same order, the child appends zero or more members after them, and every other root member of the file is unchanged. Both versions are read from the commit trees, never from the working tree. For a maintenance change the scanner omits the path from the operation lines it matches for this action in every inspection pass, both the name-status pass that synthesizes git add and git rm lines and the patch pass. Any other change to the path, every other path in the same commit, and a commit-message match keep their findings.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the one JSON file the exemption covers. Exactly one file, never a glob or a directory.

schema.description: Repository-relative path of the JSON Schema the resulting file must validate against for the change to count as maintenance.

change.description: The only maintenance shape: members appended to the collection, none removed, altered, or reordered.

collection.description: JSON Pointer to the root-level array whose members may be appended. Every other root member, including schemaVersion, must be byte-identical between the parent and child versions.
